correctness.rationale: Proof partitions all gaps into disjoint intervals, calculates their last divisible-by-p entries, and proves the maximal admissible interval gives F. The explicit signature (B,R) is 2p-periodic. Its exceptional signature has residue set {0,p-1} for odd p (trivial stabilizer), or {0,p} for even p; the remaining p-translation is excluded by explicit odd residue comparisons. The script independently evaluates 5000 quotient Frobenius numbers via coin DP and confirms 43554 branch evaluations and 119 exact periods. Finite checks are corroboration only.

The genus of a numerical semigroup counts its gaps, whereas its Frobenius number is the maximum gap; a genus formula does not imply a Frobenius formula.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Replacing the genus by the largest surviving gap is not an equivalent reformulation; two semigroups can have the same genus with different Frobenius numbers. value.rationale: The Frobenius number of numerical-semigroup quotients is a natural hard-to-express invariant; the special three-consecutive family is a canonical embedding-dimension-three test case of the recent quotient quasipolynomial program. An explicit formula on all residues together with its sharp least period improves restricted divisor formulas and identifies an exact noncollapse phenomenon. This is a complete natural infinite fixed-modulus classification, not an isolated or arbitrary numerical slice. Limits: no claim of earliest onset, general spacings, or variable-p uniform polynomial.
